pr.title: feat(browser): migrate to webview, add credentials, favorites, viewports, and device emulation
pr.body:
# feat(browser): migrate to webview, add credentials, favorites, viewports, and device emulation

## Summary

Replaces native `WebContentsView` with DOM-based `<webview>` tag to fix z-order issues where the browser overlay obscured UI elements (modals, dropdowns, command palette). Adds credential autofill with OS-level encryption, favorites start page, custom device viewports, and embedded DevTools.

## Changes

**WebContentsView → `<webview>` migration:**
- Browser content renders as `<webview>` DOM element with proper z-order
- Security hardened: `will-attach-webview` handler forces sandbox/contextIsolation, isolated `persist:browser` partition with blocked permissions
- Removed freeze/unfreeze screenshot mechanism (no longer needed)
- Simplified IPC: 15 handlers reduced to 7
- Pane focus via webview DOM focus event, pointer-events disabled during tab drag

**Embedded DevTools:**
- DevTools rendered via `WebContentsView` + `setDevToolsWebContents` (only viable approach for `<webview>`)
- Resizable divider (bottom/left) with pointer capture drag
- Persistent view (hide/show on toggle, no re-creation)

**Credential Store:**
- SQLite table with `safeStorage` encryption (macOS Keychain, Windows DPAPI)
- Auto-detect login forms via `MutationObserver` for SPA support
- Autofill icon injected into password fields with multi-account picker dropdown
- Save password modal triggered via `console.log` marker pattern (survives page redirect)
- Auth prompt before revealing passwords: Touch ID (macOS), Windows Hello via PowerShell (Windows), confirmation dialog (Linux)
- Saved Passwords management in Settings with reveal (5s auto-hide) and delete
- Page title stored with credentials for same-host disambiguation
- Port-aware domain matching (`localhost:3000` ≠ `localhost:4000`)

**Favorites & Start Page:**
- New browser shows favorites grid instead of blank page (favicon + name cards)
- Star button with host-based matching — dropdown for "Add new" or "Remove all for site"
- Right-click context menu: Edit, Duplicate (with current URL), Delete
- Drag-and-drop reorder
- Add/edit modal with editable name and URL

**Custom Viewports & Device Emulation:**
- Device emulation via Chrome DevTools Protocol (`Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`)
- 7 built-in presets (iPhone SE, 14 Pro, 14 Pro Max, iPad Mini, iPad Pro 11", Galaxy S24, Pixel 8)
- Custom viewports: add/remove in Settings > Web Browser, persisted in preferences
- Proportional scaling with `transform: scale()` when window is smaller than device
- Responsive mode toolbar dropdown with all viewports

**Browser UX:**
- Mouse back/forward buttons via `app-command` (Windows) + injected `mouseup` listener (macOS)
- "Open URLs from terminal in" setting moved to Web Browser section
- `Cmd+L` focus restricted to focused pane in split layout
- URL preserved across split/drag operations (ignore `about:blank` navigation)

## Screenshots

_Screenshots needed — please attach manually_

pr.title: feat: sync app UI theme with terminal theme
pr.body:
## What

App chrome (titlebar, sidebar, status bar, tabs, dialogs, command palette, preferences) now adopts colors from the active terminal theme. Switching themes in Appearance updates the entire UI, not just the terminal.

## Why

The app UI was hardcoded to a single dark color scheme while the terminal supported 12 themes. Users switching to e.g. Nord, Dracula, or Solarized Light got a jarring visual mismatch between the terminal and surrounding chrome.

## How it works

- `appTheme.ts` derives ~35 CSS custom properties (`--c-*`) from any `ITheme` object using the background, foreground, and ANSI color palette
- Light vs dark detection via luminance threshold (handles Solarized Light)
- Accent color adapts per theme from ANSI blue; status colors from ANSI red/green/yellow
- Reactive `$effect` in `App.svelte` applies the theme on preference change
- 49 components migrated from hardcoded `rgba()`/hex to `var(--c-*)` references
- Notch overlay intentionally retains fixed colors (renders on physical black notch)

## How to test

1. `npm run dev`
2. Open Preferences > Appearance
3. Switch between themes (Default, Dracula, Nord, Tokyo Night, Solarized Light, etc.)
4. Verify the entire app chrome updates: titlebar, sidebar, status bar, tabs, dialogs, command palette, toast notifications, welcome dashboard
5. Open a dialog (Cmd+K for palette, Cmd+, for preferences) and confirm it matches the theme
6. Try Solarized Light specifically — app should switch to light surfaces with dark text
7. Verify glassmorphism (backdrop blur) still works on all themes

## Screenshots / recordings

_UI change — screenshots recommended during review_

- [x] Code review guidelines updated to enforce `--c-*` variable usage

pr.title: feat(terminal): add tmux session persistence for shell sessions
pr.body:
## What

Shell sessions can now run inside tmux via a dedicated socket (`-L canopy`), surviving app close, crashes, and restarts. Opt-in via Terminal preferences.

## Why

When Canopy closes or crashes, all shell sessions die — running processes are lost and scrollback is gone. Tmux solves this by running a server process that owns sessions independently of the app lifecycle. Users working with long-running builds, SSH sessions, or complex terminal state benefit from sessions that persist across restarts.

## How to test

1. Open Settings > Terminal, enable "tmux session persistence"
2. Open a shell tab, run a command (e.g. `sleep 999`)
3. Quit the app (Cmd+Q) — if close policy is "Ask", choose "Keep Running"
4. Reopen the app — the shell should reattach with `sleep` still running
5. Open Cmd+K > "Tmux Sessions" — verify the session browser shows correct state
6. Kill a session from the browser — verify it disappears
7. Rename a session — verify it stays visible and attached
8. Type `exit` in a shell — verify it shows ExitBanner (not DetachedOverlay)
9. Disable tmux in preferences — verify new shells use raw PTY
10. Verify `tmux -L canopy list-sessions` from external terminal matches app state

## Checklist

pr.title: fix(terminal): prevent WebGL crash on session restore
pr.body:
## What

Defer WebGL context creation so only the active (visible) terminal gets a GPU context during mount. Inactive terminals get their context lazily when switched to.

## Why

On app startup, session restore recreates all terminals simultaneously. Each one created a WebGL context unconditionally, exceeding the browser's limit (~8-16 contexts). This caused the active terminal's context to be evicted, resulting in a crashed renderer (sad face icon, blank white terminal).

## How to test

1. Open 5+ tabs with different tools (Shell, Claude Code, etc.)
2. Quit the app
3. Relaunch — all terminals should render correctly
4. Switch between tabs — WebGL attaches/detaches on demand without crashes

## Checklist

- [x] Builds without errors (`npm run build`)
- [x] No new warnings introduced
- [ ] Tested on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Linux
- [ ] Tested on Windows

pr.title: fix(terminal): block Ctrl+Z in AI tool terminals to prevent session suspend
pr.body:
## What
Intercept Ctrl+Z in AI tool terminal sessions (Claude, Gemini, Codex, OpenCode) to prevent SIGTSTP from suspending the CLI process.

## Why
Pressing Ctrl+Z in AI CLI tools sends SIGTSTP which suspends the process. Since the user has no access to stdin afterward, `fg` cannot resume it — resulting in a dead, unrecoverable session. Fixes #69.

## How to test
1. Open an AI tool terminal (e.g. Claude)
2. Press Ctrl+Z — nothing should happen (no suspend)
3. Open a regular shell terminal
4. Press Ctrl+Z — should work normally (suspend)

pr.title: perf(session): lazy restore tabs on startup
pr.body:
## What

Only restore the last active tab on startup. All other tabs are created in a suspended state (placeholder panes, no live PTY/WebSocket) and defer spawning until the user activates them.

## Why

Restoring all tabs at once on startup is slow and resource-heavy, especially with many terminals or AI tool sessions open. This change makes startup significantly faster by only paying the cost of restoring the single active tab.

## How to test

1. Open several tabs (shell, Claude, browser, editor)
2. Quit the app and relaunch
3. Verify only the last active tab spawns a PTY (check main process logs)
4. Click a suspended tab — verify it restores and becomes functional
5. Close a suspended tab — verify no errors
6. Close the active tab when the next tab is suspended — verify it resumes
7. Drag a suspended tab to reorder — verify it works
8. Use Cmd+1-9 / Cmd+Shift+[ / ] to navigate to suspended tabs
9. Quit and relaunch again — verify suspended tabs persist correctly in layout

## Checklist

pr.title: fix(terminal): pass agent env vars to tmux sessions
pr.body:
## What

Forward agent environment variables (`CANOPY_HOOK_PORT`, `CANOPY_HOOK_TOKEN`, settings env) to `tmux new-session` via `-e` flags so the process running inside tmux receives them.

## Why

When tmux integration is enabled, `TmuxManager.newSession()` spawns the agent (e.g. Claude Code) inside a detached tmux session using only the base login environment. The hook port and auth token env vars were set on the `tmux attach` PTY instead, never reaching the actual agent process. This broke inspector hook event delivery, leaving the inspector panel empty.

## How to test

1. Enable tmux in preferences (`tmux.enabled = true`)
2. Open a Claude Code session
3. Verify the inspector panel shows live session state (status, context window, cost, tasks)
4. Compare with tmux disabled — behavior should be identical

pr.body:
## What
Fix tmux session lifecycle so sessions are properly cleaned up when panes/tabs close, dead tabs are not respawned on app restart, and projects restore in parallel with preserved sidebar ordering.

## Why
Closing tabs or panes left underlying tmux sessions alive as orphans. On app restart, stopped shells were serialized in the layout and respawned as new sessions — e.g., stopping 4 of 5 shells, quitting, and reopening would show 5 active sessions again. Projects also restored sequentially, causing visible tab flashing through each project.

## How to test
- Enable tmux persistence in Settings > Terminal
- Open multiple projects in a single window
- Stop all but one shell via the sidebar stop icon
- Verify `tmux -L canopy list-sessions` shows only 1 session
- Quit app (Cmd+Q), reopen — only 1 active session should appear
- Sidebar project order should match the order before quitting
- Close a pane in a split — the tmux session should be cleaned up
- Close a window — its tmux sessions should be killed (unless quitting with "Keep sessions running" policy)

## Checklist
- [x] Typecheck passes (`npm run typecheck`)
- [x] Lint passes (`npm run lint`)
- [x] No unrelated changes

Ensures window configs (attached projects, active worktree) are always saved before the app quits, regardless of tmux close policy. Adds diagnostic logging to the project restore lifecycle.

## Why

When `tmux.closePolicy` was set to `'ask'`, the `before-quit` handler returned early before reaching the config save, then re-entered via `app.quit()` in an infinite loop — configs were never persisted. Additionally, `setActiveWorktree` changes were only saved at quit time (not eagerly), so a crash or forced kill would lose the active worktree selection.

Separately, projects can silently disappear from the sidebar after restore with no error toast and no console trace, making the root cause hard to diagnose. Diagnostic logging is added to catch this.

## How to test

1. Attach 4+ projects to a single window
2. Quit and reopen — verify all projects appear in the sidebar
3. Set tmux policy to `ask`, quit with active tmux sessions — verify the dialog appears once (not in a loop) and all projects restore on next launch
4. Open DevTools console during restore — verify `[workspace]` debug/warn logs appear with correct counts
5. Switch between worktrees, quit, reopen — verify the correct worktree is selected (tests `setActiveWorktree` eager save)

## Checklist

- [x] Follows conventional commit format
- [x] TypeScript compiles (`npm run typecheck`)
- [x] Linter passes (`npm run lint`)
- [ ] Covered by tests
- [x] No new dependencies

pr.title: feat(ci): auto-track claude code releases for compatibility
pr.body:
## What

Adds a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that monitors `marckrenn/claude-code-changelog` for new Claude Code CLI releases, analyzes whether Canopy needs adjustments, and opens a PR with proposed changes when relevant.

## Why

Claude Code is a core integration for our CI workflows (code review, PR validation, audits, bug triage) and our `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` runtime dependency. New CLI releases can change feature flags, env vars, hooks, permission models, or system prompts in ways that affect how we invoke Claude or what we tell it to do. Today we'd only catch breakage reactively. This automation gives us a continuous feedback loop on upstream changes without manual monitoring.

## How to test

1. Manually dispatch the workflow from the Actions tab with `from_version=v2.1.95` to force a check against a recent past version.
2. Confirm the workflow fetches release notes for the missed versions and runs Claude Code analysis with the prompt from `.github/prompts/claude-code-compat.md`.
3. Verify it either creates a `chore/claude-code-compat` PR with structured analysis OR writes "no changes needed" to the step summary.
4. Verify `.github/claude-code-version.json` is updated and committed to `next` with a `[skip ci]` message.
5. Dispatch again with no input — should early-exit since the tracker now matches latest.
6. (Optional) When a new Claude Code release lands while the compat PR is still open, verify the workflow pushes incremental commits to the existing PR rather than creating a duplicate.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [ ] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default)
- [x] Cross-platform: no hardcoded OS-specific labels, paths, or shell commands
- [ ] Keyboard accessible (all interactive elements reachable via keyboard)
- [ ] IPC follows \`feature:action\` naming and uses \`invoke\`/\`handle\`
- [ ] Renderer code does not import Node.js modules directly

_Feature-flag, keyboard, IPC, and renderer items are N/A — this is a CI-only change._

pr.title: feat(updater): configurable auto-update check frequency
pr.body:
## What
Adds a "Check frequency" dropdown in Preferences → Updates letting users
pick how often the app checks for updates: hourly, daily (default),
weekly, or never (manual only).

## Why
Until now the app checked for updates exactly once per launch, with no
way to opt into more frequent checks for long-running sessions or to opt
out entirely. Users on the `next` channel in particular wanted a way to
pick up pre-releases without restarting, and some users want no
automatic checks at all.

## How
- New `update.checkFrequency` preference key (`'never' | 'hourly' | 'daily' | 'weekly'`, default `'daily'`).
- Main process manages a single `setInterval` timer via `scheduleRecurringUpdateCheck()`, rescheduled through a new `app:setUpdateCheckFrequency` IPC handler whenever the pref changes.
- Picking `never` disables both the startup check *and* the recurring check — only the manual "Check for updates" button works.
- Timer is cleared on `before-quit` (both the normal path and the Squirrel update-install path) to avoid leaks.
- Frequency normalization uses `ts-pattern` with `.exhaustive()` for compile-time safety.

## How to test
1. Open Preferences → Updates → confirm new "Check frequency" dropdown with Every hour / Every day / Every week / Never options; default is "Every day".
2. Change the value — it persists across restarts (check via SQLite `preferences` table: `update.checkFrequency`).
3. Set to "Never" in a packaged build → restart → no startup update check fires; manual "Check for updates" button still works.
4. Set to "Every hour" → verify a `checkForUpdates` call after the interval elapses (can tail main-process logs or temporarily lower `HOUR_MS` to a few seconds for quicker verification).
5. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run svelte-check` both pass with 0 errors.

## Screenshots / recordings
_Preferences → Updates now shows a third row "Check frequency" with a dropdown between the existing "Update channel" select and the "Check for updates" button._

## Checklist
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run svelte-check` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [ ] Manual QA on macOS packaged build
- [x] No breaking changes to existing preferences schema

pr.title: ci: auto-fix workflow with label, review, and @claude triggers
pr.body:
## What

Renames the `audit-fix` workflow to `auto-fix` and reworks its trigger surface: it now runs on any PR via four explicit entry points — the `auto-fix` label, `claude[bot]` review submissions, human "Request changes" reviews, and human comments (top-level or inline) mentioning `@claude`. Per-PR concurrency with `cancel-in-progress: true` guarantees only the latest run is active on any given PR.

## Why

The old `audit-fix` workflow was implicit (fired on every `claude[bot]` review) and narrow (only PRs whose branch started with `audit/`), and used an `audit-fixes-applied` marker label to avoid loops. We want intentional, label-and-mention-driven auto-fix that works on any PR and gives reviewers a direct `@claude …` handoff.

## How to test

Pre-merge this is workflow YAML only — real validation happens on the first post-merge run.

1. Merge into `next`.
2. Manually create the label: `gh label create auto-fix --description "Trigger Claude auto-fix workflow on this PR" --color FBCA04`.
3. On any PR, add the `auto-fix` label → confirm `Auto Fix` run starts and the label-name branch of the `if:` is taken.
4. Wait for `Code Review` to post a `claude[bot]` review on a PR → confirm `Auto Fix` auto-triggers via the review path.
5. As a human, submit a "Request changes" review on a PR → confirm `Auto Fix` triggers. Submit a plain "Comment" review → confirm it does **not** trigger.
6. Post a top-level PR comment `@claude please tighten this error message` → confirm `Auto Fix` triggers, the `Resolve PR context` step resolves the head ref, and Claude fetches the triggering comment via `gh api` and replies with `gh pr comment`.
7. Leave an inline review-line comment containing `@claude` → confirm the same behaviour.
8. While a run is in progress on a PR, re-add the label → confirm the first run is cancelled and the second supersedes it (concurrency \`cancel-in-progress\`).
9. Negative: post a comment without \`@claude\` → no trigger. Submit an \`approved\` human review → no trigger. Add an unrelated label → no trigger.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [ ] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default)
- [x] Cross-platform: no hardcoded OS-specific labels, paths, or shell commands
- [ ] Keyboard accessible (all interactive elements reachable via keyboard)
- [ ] IPC follows \`feature:action\` naming and uses \`invoke\`/\`handle\`
- [ ] Renderer code does not import Node.js modules directly

## What

Add a "From existing branch" mode to the Create Worktree dialog that
checks out any local or remote-only branch into a new worktree in one
step. Remote-only picks (e.g. `origin/feature-x`) are created as local
tracking branches automatically.

## Why

Previously the Create Worktree flow only supported creating a new branch
off a base. Users wanting to check out an existing branch (e.g. a
teammate's PR branch from `origin`) had to drop to the terminal. This
closes that gap without adding clicks for the default new-branch flow.

## How to test

Preconditions: a repo with local `feature/foo`, a remote-only
`origin/feature-remote`, and `origin/main` shadowing local `main`.

1. Open the Create Worktree dialog from the sidebar — confirm the
   segmented `[New branch] [From existing branch]` toggle is visible
   with "New branch" active by default.
2. **Regression:** in "New branch" mode, pick a base, type a name,
   Enter → worktree created, click count matches today.
3. Switch to "From existing branch" → label becomes "Branch to check
   out", no naming step.
4. Select `feature/foo` → Create → `git -C <worktree> branch
   --show-current` = `feature/foo`, no new branch created.
5. Select `origin/feature-remote` (shows "(remote only)" tag) → Create
   → new worktree has local `feature-remote` tracking
   `origin/feature-remote`.
6. Select `origin/main` (no "(remote only)" tag, because local `main`
   exists) → Create → reuses local `main`, no "branch already exists".
7. Attempt to check out `main` while it's already checked out in the
   main worktree → expect a clear error message in the dialog.
8. In existing mode, type a search query, ArrowDown, Enter → immediate

9. **Regression:** task-tracker "New branch" flow via

pr.body:
## What
Add a JetBrains Rider-inspired run configurations system. Users define commands in `.canopy/run.toml` files per project/subproject, then run them via sidebar, titlebar toolbar, or a manager dialog.

## Why
Developers working in monorepos need a quick way to start dev servers, build scripts, and other project commands without typing them manually each time. Configurations are stored in the repo so the team can share them.

## How to test
1. Create `.canopy/run.toml` in any project directory:
   ```toml
   [[configurations]]
   name = "Dev Server"
   command = "npm"
   args = "run dev"
   max_instances = 1
   ```
2. Open the project in Canopy — RUN section appears in sidebar
3. Click Play (▶) → terminal tab opens with the command running
4. Click Stop (■) → process killed, tab reflects exit
5. Open titlebar dropdown → each config has inline Play/Stop
6. Click Settings (⚙) → manager dialog with tree + inline editor
7. Try running a `max_instances = 1` config twice → toast blocks it
8. Switch worktree → running processes scoped per worktree

pr.title: ci: proactively auto-fix bug-labeled issues via agent
pr.body:
## What

Adds a new `Bug Auto-Fix` GitHub Actions workflow that triggers when an
issue is opened or labeled with `bug`. It spawns Claude Code to read the
report, investigate the codebase, and — if confident — apply a minimal
fix on a `claude/auto-fix/issue-<N>` branch and open a PR against `next`
that closes the issue. When the agent isn't confident enough, it posts a
short diagnostic comment on the issue instead.

## Why

Complements the existing agent automation:

- `bug-assign.yml` finds a likely human author for new bug reports.
- `auto-fix.yml` applies fixes to PRs based on review comments.

Neither attempts to actually fix a bug report proactively. This fills
that gap — small, well-scoped bugs can get a PR ready for human review
within minutes, and ambiguous ones get a triage comment that saves the
next human some investigation time.

## How to test

1. Merge this PR (or push the branch to a fork) so the workflow is
   registered.
2. Open a new issue via the Bug Report template — it will auto-apply
   the \`bug\` label. Describe a small, localized bug (e.g. a wrong
   string, an off-by-one in a pure function).
3. Watch the **Actions** tab → \`Bug Auto-Fix\` run. Confirm:
   - It checks out \`next\`.
   - It stays inside the tool allowlist (no tools denied).
4. Verify the outcome:
   - **If the agent fixes it:** a new PR titled \`fix: … (#N)\` targets
     \`next\`, body contains \`Fixes #N\`, and \`npm run format/lint/typecheck\`
     all ran. Review the diff before merging.
   - **If the agent declines:** a short diagnostic comment appears on
     the issue with files investigated and why it stopped. No branch or
     PR is created.
5. **Assignee skip test:** open a \`bug\` issue and assign it to a human
   before the workflow finishes — the agent should abort silently.
6. **Duplicate protection test:** remove and re-add the \`bug\` label.
   The concurrency group cancels the in-flight run; the agent's
   existing-branch/PR check prevents a duplicate PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Conventional commit prefix (\`ci:\`)
- [x] YAML validated locally (\`js-yaml\` parses clean)
- [x] Tool allowlist scoped to \`git\`, \`gh\`, \`npm run {lint,format,typecheck,svelte-check}\` — no blanket \`Bash\`
- [x] Honors \`CLAUDE.md\` rules in the agent prompt (conventional commits, neverthrow, ts-pattern, no renderer-side Node imports, no \`SPEC.md\`)
- [x] No app code changed — CI/automation only

pr.title: feat(remote): WebRTC remote control via QR pairing (beta)
pr.body:
## What
Add a beta remote control feature that lets a phone, tablet, or another laptop mirror and control a Canopy desktop session over local WiFi by scanning a QR code. Opens a WebRTC peer connection with three data channels (commands / state / stream) for typed RPC, live state mirroring, and PTY output streaming.

## Why
Workflows that start on a desktop often need to check in from another device — review tab output from the couch, tail a long-running agent from a phone, kick off a build from a tablet during a meeting. Switching machines or SSH-ing around is friction; a QR scan is not. This feature keeps the full Canopy workspace (projects, tabs, PTYs, agents) mirrored to any LAN-reachable device without tunneling or cloud services, and stays opt-in + off by default for users who don't want the extra network surface.

## How to test

### Enable the feature
1. Open **Settings → Remote Control** → enable the toggle.
2. Pick an action-guard profile (recommended: `destructive`).

### Basic pair flow
3. Command palette → **Open Remote Connection (Beta)**.
4. Scan the QR with an iPhone/iPad/Android/other laptop on the same WiFi.
5. Approve the device on desktop (optionally check **Remember this device**).
6. Verify: phone renders the project list, you can open tabs, type into shell/Claude, switch worktrees.

### Trusted device reconnect
7. With "Remember this device" set, close + reopen the remote client. It should auto-pair without a modal prompt.
8. Remove the device from **Settings → Remote Control → Trusted Devices** and reconnect — manual accept should be required again.

### Terminal resize
9. On mobile, tap the inline terminal. PTY should reshape to the phone's viewport (shell prompt fits on screen, no horizontal scroll).
10. Click the terminal on desktop — PTY should reclaim desktop dimensions.

### Mobile UX
11. Tap into an inline terminal while the keyboard is visible — the layout should shrink to sit above the keyboard, not be hidden underneath.
12. Check the fullscreen terminal overlay (tap the expand icon on a tab row).
13. Tap the **+ New tool** button on mobile — bottom sheet opens with the tool list.

### Beta surfaces
14. "Beta" badge visible in: command palette entry, Remote Control preferences section, Remote Connection modal title, and the peer client topbar.

### Cache / refresh
15. Pair, refresh the phone page. It should auto-reconnect without getting stuck on "connecting to host".
16. Open Remote Control from command palette twice without stopping the session — second open should adopt the live state instead of erroring.

## Screenshots / recordings
_TBD — add screenshots of: QR modal with icon + green corners, trusted devices list in preferences, mobile workspace view, fullscreen terminal overlay._

pr.title: fix(workspace): clean up stale project rows on startup restore
pr.body:
Closes #128

## What

On startup, filter restored project paths against the filesystem. Drop any whose directory no longer exists, remove the stale rows from the SQLite `workspaces` + `workspace_layouts` tables, rewrite the `openWindowConfigs` preference, and surface a single aggregated toast listing what was cleaned up.

## Why

Closes itsoltech/canopy-desktop#128. When a project's directory was deleted or moved on disk, the next launch hit `Failed to restore: <name>` every time. The stale row stayed in `workspaces`, the path stayed in `openWindowConfigs`, and because the project never mounted in the sidebar there was no UI path to detach it — the only workaround was hand-editing the SQLite DB.

## How to test

1. `npm run dev`
2. Attach a test project, e.g. create an empty dir and run `git init` in it, then attach it in Canopy.
3. Quit Canopy.
4. Delete the test directory from disk.
5. Relaunch Canopy.
6. Expect: a single toast `Removed 1 stale project (folder missing): <name>`. No "Failed to restore" toast.
7. Verify the row is gone: `sqlite3 ~/Library/Application\ Support/Canopy/*.db 'SELECT path FROM workspaces;'` — no stale entry.
8. Verify the preference is clean: `sqlite3 ~/Library/Application\ Support/Canopy/*.db "SELECT value FROM preferences WHERE key='openWindowConfigs';"` — no stale path.
9. Relaunch once more — expect no toast at all.

Regression checks:

- Restore with all valid paths → normal restore, no toast.
- Window with one stale + one valid path → window opens with the valid project only, toast appears once, saved bounds honored.
- Multiple windows with stale paths → exactly one aggregated toast, not one per window.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [ ] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default)
- [x] Cross-platform: no hardcoded OS-specific labels, paths, or shell commands
- [x] Keyboard accessible (all interactive elements reachable via keyboard)
- [x] IPC follows `feature:action` naming and uses `invoke`/`handle`
- [x] Renderer code does not import Node.js modules directly

pr.title: feat: add toggleable cpu/ram hud in status bar
pr.body:
## What

Adds an opt-in indicator in the bottom-right status bar that shows total app CPU and resident memory (aggregated across main, renderer, GPU, and utility processes). Toggled via Preferences → General; clicking the HUD opens the same settings page.

## Why

We already had dev-only perf diagnostics behind `CANOPY_PERF=1`, but no always-available way for users to see how much Canopy is consuming. The main constraint was that the HUD itself must not become a resource hog.

## How to test

1. `npm run dev`
2. Confirm the status bar looks unchanged (HUD off by default).
3. Open Preferences → General → enable "Show CPU and RAM usage in status bar".
4. Verify the HUD appears in the bottom-right as `X% · Y MB` and updates roughly once per second. Numbers should track Activity Monitor.
5. Click the HUD — Preferences → General opens.
6. Disable the toggle — HUD disappears immediately. Confirm via Activity Monitor that the main process returns to idle baseline (sampler stops).
7. Reload the renderer (Cmd-R) with the HUD on — subscription re-registers cleanly, no leftover intervals.
8. Restart the app — pref persists.

## Perf safeguards

- Sampling interval only runs while at least one renderer is subscribed; toggle off → `clearInterval` → zero overhead.
- 1 Hz sampling via `app.getAppMetrics()` (single synchronous call).
- Last payload is memoized — if rounded `cpu`/`memMb` values are unchanged the IPC send and downstream DOM update are skipped entirely.
- Per-window cleanup via `webContents.once('destroyed')` so reloads and window closes don't leak subscriptions.
- `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the HUD so digit width changes don't trigger layout thrash.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [x] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default)
- [x] Cross-platform: no hardcoded OS-specific labels, paths, or shell commands
- [x] Keyboard accessible (all interactive elements reachable via keyboard)
- [x] IPC follows `feature:action` naming and uses `invoke`/`handle`
- [x] Renderer code does not import Node.js modules directly

pr.title: feat(agents): add Codex agent integration
pr.body:
## What

Full hook-based integration for OpenAI Codex CLI, matching the existing Claude Code and Gemini adapters. Codex sessions now get real-time status tracking, inspector data, preferences UI, and session resume.

## Why

Codex was registered as a tool but ran as a plain CLI without hook integration — no status tracking, no inspector, no session context injection, no resume on app restart.

## How it works

- **Hooks setup**: Writes to project-level `.codex/hooks.json` (Codex has no `--settings` flag or config home env var). Merges with existing hooks, refcounts concurrent sessions per worktree, restores original on cleanup. Enables hooks via `--enable codex_hooks` CLI flag.
- **5 hook events**: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop — normalized to the shared event schema.
- **Session resume**: `buildResumeArgs` returns `['resume', sessionId]` (Codex uses a subcommand, not a flag).
- **Inspector**: CodexExtras component shows turn count, working directory, transcript path, and last assistant response.
- **Preferences**: Model, approval mode, sandbox, full-auto, profile, API key, base URL, custom env vars, settings JSON override.

## How to test

1. `npm run dev`, spawn Codex from the tool picker
2. Verify dev console shows `[agent-hook] SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, etc.
3. Check inspector panel shows model, permission mode, tool calls, turns, CWD

pr.title: feat: crash detection with GitHub issue reporting
pr.body:
## What

Detect app crashes and show a dialog on next launch with crash details and a "Create issue" button that opens a pre-filled GitHub issue.

## Why

No crash detection existed. When the app crashed, users had no way to report what happened or help us reproduce the problem.

## How it works

- **Sentinel file** (`.canopy-running` in userData): created on startup, removed on graceful quit. If present at next launch, the app crashed.
- **Exception handlers**: `uncaughtException`, `unhandledRejection`, `render-process-gone`, `child-process-gone` write detailed crash data to `crash-report.json`.
- **Crash dialog**: on next launch, if crash data exists, a modal shows timestamp, error type, version info, and stack trace with "Dismiss" and "Create issue" buttons.
- **GitHub issue**: "Create issue" opens the browser with a pre-filled issue (title, body with crash metadata, `bug` + `crash` labels). Stack traces truncated to 3000 chars for URL length safety.
- **Production only**: gated behind `app.isPackaged` to avoid false positives during development.

## How to test

1. Build a production build (`npm run build`)
2. Launch the app, then force-kill it (`kill -9 <pid>`)
3. Relaunch - crash report dialog should appear
4. Click "Create issue" - browser opens GitHub with pre-filled issue
5. Click "Dismiss" - dialog closes, does not reappear on next launch
6. Normal quit + relaunch - no crash dialog

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [x] No new dependencies added
- [x] Follows existing IPC, preload bridge, and dialog patterns
- [ ] Tested in production build

pr.title: fix(terminal): debounce resize to prevent flickering
pr.body:
## What
Debounce terminal resize handling to eliminate content flickering and RAM
spikes during window resize and panel toggles.

## Why
ResizeObserver fired fitAddon.fit() synchronously on every container size
change — up to 60 times/second during drag. Each fit forced the WebGL addon
to reallocate textures, causing a visible blank flash and memory pressure
from deferred GC.

## How to test
1. `npm run dev`
2. Drag the window edge to resize continuously — terminal content should
   stay visible (no blank flash), RAM should stay stable
3. Toggle sidebar and inspector panel — terminal should refit after ~80ms
   with no flicker
4. Resize split panes — divider drag should feel smooth
5. Verify terminal output alignment after resize (run `ls`, resize, check
   columns still line up)

## What

## Why
Codex and Gemini CLIs execute hook commands via the Windows system shell, which resolves `.sh` files through file associations. If `.sh` is associated with Git Bash or WSL bash (common on Windows), every hook event spawns a new visible terminal window — resulting in 100+ open windows per command cycle. Claude Code CLI is exempt because it runs `.sh` hooks via bash internally on Windows.

2. Open a Codex session in Canopy.

pr.body:
## What

Split `pty.write` and `agent.sendInput` out of `DESTRUCTIVE_METHODS` into a new `SESSION_GRANTABLE_METHODS` set. In `destructive` and `full` action-guard profiles these now prompt the host once per peer session (`Allow for session`), then auto-allow every subsequent call until the peer disconnects.

## Why

The `destructive` action-guard profile was effectively unusable: every keystroke in a remote terminal fired a confirm dialog because `pty.write` lived in `DESTRUCTIVE_METHODS`. `full` had the same problem. Security posture is preserved — the host still has to approve terminal access explicitly — but the prompt happens once per session instead of per keystroke.

Closes #136

## How to test

1. Pair a remote device; leave the profile at the default `destructive`.
2. Open a remote terminal on the peer and start typing → expect **exactly one** `Remote session access request` dialog ("Allow for session"), then fluent keystrokes.
3. Close a tab from the peer → expect the existing per-call `Remote action request` dialog (destructive path still works).
4. Disconnect the peer, reconnect, type again → expect a fresh session-grant dialog (grants cleared on `HostRpcServer.dispose`).
5. Switch profile to `full` and repeat steps 2-4 → same session-grant behaviour for `pty.write`; other methods still prompt per-call.
6. Switch profile to `none` → zero dialogs.

- [x] `npm run build` clean

pr.title: fix(git): coalesce GitWatcher refreshes to fix shutdown crash (#147)
pr.body:
## What

Coalesce overlapping `GitWatcher` refresh batches so concurrent `.git/` events no longer stack fresh `git` subprocess batches on top. Also add a `process.on('exit')` fallback that clears the crash sentinel on any normal exit.

## Why

Fixes #147. `GitWatcher` had no in-flight guard: every debounced refresh spawned up to 4 concurrent `git` processes (`simple-git`). Under Windows antivirus I/O pressure, each batch could take seconds, and new `.git/` events kept stacking more batches on top — producing a subprocess pileup that left the app unresponsive, forcing users to Task-Manager-kill it. The sentinel was left behind, producing an `ungracefulShutdown` crash report on next launch.

Two tight changes:

1. `GitWatcher` coalesces new events into a single tail-dispatched pass instead of launching overlapping batches, and a `stopped` flag blocks new work after teardown.
2. `process.on('exit')` → `clearSentinel()` safety net covers the `before-quit` async dialog paths that `preventDefault()` and return early (active-session confirm, tmux close-policy).

## How to test

1. `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build` — all green.
2. `npm run dev`, open a workspace on the canopy repo, then in a terminal run `for i in (seq 1 20); git commit --allow-empty -m t$i; end` and watch `ps -ef | rg '[c]anopy.*git '`. Subprocess count should plateau at ~4 instead of spiking into the dozens.
3. Kill the dev app with `kill -TERM <main pid>`, relaunch, verify no `ungracefulShutdown` dialog appears and `~/Library/Application Support/canopy-code/.canopy-running` is gone.

pr.title: fix(crash): sync untracked-diff reads, recover macos .ips stacks
pr.body:
## What

Three commits addressing #150:

1. **`fix(crash):`** macOS `CrashReporter.init()` now scans
   `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` for a recent `Canopy-*.ips` whose
   mtime post-dates the previous sentinel and attaches the triggered
   thread's symbolicated stack + exception info to `crash-report.json`.
   New module `src/main/crash/NativeCrashReader.ts`.
2. **`fix(git):`** `GitRepository.buildUntrackedDiffFile` switched from
   `fs.promises.readFile` to `readFileSync`. This is the root-cause fix.
3. **`fix(fs):`** `fs:readFile` IPC handler switched from
   `fs.promises.open`/`read`/`close` to `openSync`/`readSync`/`closeSync`.
   Defensive — same class of bug, different (user-triggered) call site.

## Why

#150 was filed as an `ungracefulShutdown` report with the message
"The app did not shut down cleanly" and no stack. The user attached the
real macOS `.ips` dump, which showed a native crash on Thread 0
`CrBrowserMain` ~4.7 h after launch in Background role:

```
EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP) brk 0
…
node::fs::FileHandle::CloseReq::Resolve()
node::MakeLibuvRequestCallback<uv_fs_s, …>::Wrapper
uv__work_done → uv__io_poll → uv_run
```

The crash had nothing to do with shutdown — the sentinel-only detector
mislabels every native runtime crash as "ungracefulShutdown" because
the sentinel is still on disk on next launch. We were blind to what
was actually happening.

**Root cause (fix 2):** `ChangesPanel.svelte` and `DiffPane.svelte`
both subscribe to `onFilesChanged` (200 ms debounce) **and**
`onGitChanged`, and they stay mounted via `class:hidden` (CSS-only),
so subscriptions remain active even when the panel is not visible and
even when the window is in the background. Each event fires
`window.api.gitDiff()` → `GitRepository.getDiffParsed()` →
`Promise.all(buildUntrackedDiffFile)` — N parallel
`fs.promises.readFile` calls per refresh cycle, one per untracked
file. Each `readFile` allocates a JS `FileHandle` whose async close
goes through `FileHandle::CloseReq::Resolve()`. Over hours of
unattended background file activity (build watch, AI agent edits, git
fetch, etc.) this exposes a V8 CHECK race in Electron 41 that aborts
the process. Sync read removes the JS `FileHandle` allocation entirely
from the hot path. Untracked working-copy files are typically few and
small, so the read is cheap.

**Diagnostics (fix 1):** the next time someone hits a native runtime
crash on macOS, the report will contain the actual triggered-thread
stack and exception type instead of "did not shut down cleanly".

**Defensive (fix 3):** the only other JS-side `FileHandle` in `src/main`
is the `fs:readFile` IPC handler used by the file-preview pane. Same
class of bug, sync trio fixes it without affecting partial-read
behaviour.

Refs #150.

## How to test

1. `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build` — green.
2. **Diff hot path:** open a workspace with at least one untracked file,
   show the Changes tab, then trigger filesystem activity in the repo:
   ```fish
   for i in (seq 1 50); touch test_$i.txt; sleep 0.05; rm test_$i.txt; end
   ```
   The Changes panel should keep updating without errors. Verify the
   list of untracked files renders correctly and the diff content for
   each is shown.
3. **File preview:** click a file in the file tree to preview it.
   Verify small text files, large text files (≥1 MB), and binary files
   all behave as before. Verify `truncated: true` is set when the file
   exceeds 1 MB.
4. **Native crash recovery (macOS):** with a packaged build, force a
   main-process crash (`process.abort()` from a dev menu item, or
   `kill -SEGV <main_pid>`). Confirm a fresh `Canopy-*.ips` lands in
   `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/`. Relaunch the app — the Crash
   Report dialog should display the symbolicated native stack instead
   of "The app did not shut down cleanly", and
   `~/Library/Application Support/canopy-code/crash-report.json`
   should contain `stack` plus a `nativeCrash` object with
   `exceptionType`, `triggeredThread`, `incidentId`, `sourceFile`.
5. **Negative path:** delete every `Canopy-*.ips` from
   `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/` (and `Retired/`),
   `touch ~/Library/Application\ Support/canopy-code/.canopy-running`
   to simulate a stale sentinel without a matching dump, relaunch,
   verify the report falls back to the original "The app did not shut
   down cleanly" message with no stack.
6. **Non-macOS:** Linux/Windows behaviour is unchanged — the reader
   returns `null` on `process.platform !== 'darwin'`.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [ ] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default) — N/A,
      bug fix
- [x] Cross-platform: no hardcoded OS-specific labels, paths, or shell
      commands (macOS-only path is gated behind `process.platform`)
- [x] Keyboard accessible — N/A, no UI changes
- [x] IPC follows `feature:action` naming and uses `invoke`/`handle` —
      no IPC changes
- [x] Renderer code does not import Node.js modules directly — N/A
- [x] Feature docs in `docs/` updated

      `.ips` recovery path and the `nativeCrash` field shape)

pr.title: fix(updater): allow pre-release users to update to newer stable
pr.body:
## What
When a user on the pre-release channel was on a prerelease (e.g. `0.11.0-next.8`) and a newer stable shipped (e.g. `0.11.0`), the update check failed with an error in the banner instead of installing the stable. This ties `autoUpdater.allowPrerelease` to the resolved effective channel so the updater drops down to stable cleanly.

## Why
`resolveUpdateChannel()` already correctly returns `'latest'` when stable ≥ newest prerelease, but `checkWithChannelResolution` was unconditionally setting `allowPrerelease = true` in the `next` branch. That combination (`channel='latest'` + `allowPrerelease=true`) puts electron-updater's `GitHubProvider.getLatestVersion()` into its prerelease iteration loop with `currentChannel='latest'`, which is hardcoded to only match `null`/`alpha`/`beta`. The loop walks every release, picks none, and throws — surfaced as "Update failed: …" in the banner. Pre-release users therefore got stuck on `0.11.0-next.8` once `0.11.0` shipped.

With `allowPrerelease = false` when riding down, electron-updater takes the simple else branch (`getLatestTagName()` → `/releases/latest`), finds `v0.11.0`, fetches `latest-mac.yml`, and updates normally.

## How to test
Manual end-to-end on a packaged build (no automated tests for this path):

1. Pin a packaged build to `0.11.0-next.8`, set Preferences → Updates → channel = "Pre-release".
2. Trigger "Check for Updates…". On `main` this errors. With this fix, it should find `0.11.0`, download, and offer restart.
3. Regression sweep on the patched build:
   - Stable channel on `0.11.0` → no update.
   - Pre-release channel on `0.11.0` with a newer `0.12.0-next.1` → updates to `0.12.0-next.1`.
   - Pre-release channel on `0.11.0-next.8` with a newer `0.11.0-next.9` (no newer stable) → updates to `0.11.0-next.9`.
4. Offline check (block `api.github.com`): `resolveUpdateChannel` falls back to `'next'`, `allowPrerelease` stays `true` — same behavior as before, no regression.

## Checklist
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes
- [ ] Manually verified on a packaged build against a real GitHub release (requires a published `0.11.0` against an installed `0.11.0-next.8` — not done in the worktree)

pr.title: fix(credentials): cache auth and decrypted credentials per session
pr.body:
## What

Caches both the OS auth state and decrypted credentials per Canopy
session, so password autofill stops re-prompting on every click.

## Why

Closes #156. Previously, every autofill triggered a fresh Touch ID /
Windows Hello / Linux dialog (`systemPreferences.promptTouchID`). On top
of that, after any rebuild that changes the Electron binary signature,
macOS also shows a Keychain prompt for the "canopy Safe Storage" item on
every `safeStorage.decryptString()` call — a single autofill could surface
2–3 dialogs. Expected behavior is to match Chrome: once per session.

## How

- Module-level flag `credentialSessionAuthenticated` in
  `src/main/ipc/handlers.ts` — set after first successful OS auth,
  checked on subsequent calls.
- Module-level `Map<id, Credential>` `credentialSessionCache` —
  populated after first successful decrypt; subsequent autofills skip
  both the OS prompt and `safeStorage` entirely.
- Handler now calls `CredentialStore.getById()` instead of
  `getForDomain().filter()`, so even on a cache miss only the requested
  credential is decrypted (one `safeStorage` call, not N).
- Cache invalidated in `credentials:save` / `credentials:delete` /
  `settings:import` so stale plaintext is never returned.
- Everything lives in memory only — cleared on app quit.

## How to test

1. `npm run build` (or `npm run dev`) on this branch.
2. In the browser pane, have credentials saved for 2+ different sites.
3. First autofill in a session → Touch ID prompt **once**; optionally a
   Keychain prompt for `canopy Safe Storage` once (cleared permanently
   by clicking "Always Allow").
4. Autofill the same credential again → zero prompts.
5. Autofill a different saved credential in the same session → no
   Touch ID prompt (flag reuse).
6. Edit/delete a credential in Settings → next autofill prompts again
   (cache cleared).
7. Restart Canopy → back to first-time behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] Typecheck + build pass (`npm run build` — EXIT 0)
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/integrations/browser.md`)
- [x] Manual test on macOS
- [ ] Manual test on Windows

pr.title: fix(terminal): prevent buffer corruption on tab switch
pr.body:
## What

Write PTY output through to xterm regardless of tab visibility, and resync the renderer + PTY dimensions when a hidden tab becomes visible.

## Why

Hidden tabs queued PTY output in a 2 MB `pendingData` string instead of applying it to xterm. When a long-running TUI (e.g. lazygit) exceeded the cap, the head was silently truncated — on show, xterm replayed incremental cursor-positioning deltas onto a stale buffer, producing overlapping / row-shifted text. Window resize masked the bug because TUIs full-redraw on SIGWINCH.

`ResizeObserver` on a `display:none` container also never saw a size change, so a window resize while a tab was hidden left xterm's cols/rows out of sync with the new viewport on show.

## How to test

1. `npm run dev`
2. Open two terminal tabs. In tab A run `lazygit`.
3. Switch to tab B, idle for ~1 minute (or run a command that emits a lot of output).
4. Switch back to tab A — LazyGit renders cleanly, no row shift or text overlap, no window resize needed.
5. Rapidly switch tabs 10+ times — stays clean.
6. Repeat with `vim`, `htop`, `claude`.
7. Resize the window while tab A is hidden, then switch back — content should match the new window size.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext

pr.title: fix(notch): restore mouse passthrough during peek notification
pr.body:
## What

Removes the unconditional `setIgnoreMouseEvents(false)` call that fired on every peek notification, and drops the `isPeeking` guard that prevented passthrough from being restored on mouseleave.

## Why

On macOS, `setIgnoreMouseEvents(false)` makes the **entire** window rect (560×650px) capture mouse events — including fully transparent areas. This blocked all user input across the notch overlay for up to 4 seconds on every agent status notification peek.

The fix relies on the fact that `{ forward: true }` already forwards `mousemove`/`mouseenter`/`mouseleave` to the renderer while events are ignored. Hover detection therefore works without flipping `setIgnoreMouseEvents` to false — that only needs to happen when the cursor is actually over the island (handled by `handleMouseEnter`).

## How to test

1. Open the app with an active agent session so the notch shows.
2. Trigger a peek-worthy event (agent completes, hits an error, or requests permission).
3. While the notification peeks (4 s window): click anywhere **below** the notification in the transparent overlay area — the click should reach the window behind it normally.
4. Move cursor over the notification island while it's peeking — it should expand and be interactive.
5. Click a notification row while hovering → session focuses correctly.
6. Move cursor off the island while peek is still active → clicks in the transparent area pass through immediately.

## Screenshots / recordings

UI-only behaviour change (no visual difference in the notification itself).

- [x] Follows existing code patterns

pr.title: fix(browser): restore autofill click + reload prompt under Electron 41
pr.body:
## What

Two related regressions that surfaced after the upgrade to Electron 41:
clicking a saved credential in the browser pane's autofill picker, and pressing **Cmd/Ctrl+R** (or the toolbar reload) on pages with a `beforeunload` handler. Closes #189.

## Why

- Electron 35 reshaped the `<webview>` `console-message` event. The renderer's single listener for `__CANOPY_*` IPC channels (`__CANOPY_FILL__`, `__CANOPY_CREDS_READY__`, `__CANOPY_NAV__`, `__CANOPY_PW_FIELD_FOUND__`) silently rejected the new payload, breaking autofill click, capture-on-submit, mouse back/forward, and password-field detection.
- Electron has no built-in `beforeunload` prompt. Without a `will-prevent-unload` listener, every reload on a page that returns from `beforeunload` was silently cancelled — Cmd+R looked dead. We now show the same generic dialog Chrome / Firefox / Safari show ("Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved."). Per-site custom text is intentionally not surfaced — every modern browser has ignored it since ~2017 as a phishing mitigation.

## How to test

### Autofill click

1. In Settings → Saved Logins, add a credential for any site (or capture one via the in-page banner on the next login).
2. Open the browser pane (`Cmd/Ctrl+T` → browser tab) and navigate to that site's login page.
3. Click the small key icon that appears next to the password field. Confirm the dropdown lists the saved accounts.
4. Click an account. **Expected:** username and password fields fill in immediately and the dropdown closes.

### Capture on submit (same console-message channel)

1. Log in to a new site with credentials Canopy doesn't have. The "Save password?" prompt should appear after submit.

### Mouse back / forward (same channel)

1. Navigate forward a couple of pages in the browser pane.
2. Press the mouse's back / forward buttons (or trackpad equivalents) — webview should navigate.

### Reload prompt

1. Open the browser pane, navigate to a page that runs `window.addEventListener('beforeunload', e => e.returnValue = '')` (e.g. an editing UI like Google Docs while typing, or a form with `<input>` changes that pages register).
2. Press **Cmd/Ctrl+R** or click the reload button in the toolbar.
3. **Expected:** native dialog "Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved." with **Leave** / **Stay** buttons.
   - **Leave** → page reloads.
   - **Stay** → page stays, no reload.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run svelte-check` passes
- [x] `npm run build` passes
- [x] Tested manually on macOS
- [ ] Tested on Windows
- [ ] Tested on Linux

pr.title: refactor(ui): migrate renderer to Tailwind CSS
pr.body:
## What

Migrates the entire Svelte renderer (and the remote-control mobile client) to Tailwind CSS v4. Token system in `tokens.css` rewritten to a single `@theme` block (`--color-*`, `--text-*`, `--font-weight-*`, `--leading-*`, `--tracking-*`, `--radius-*`, `--shadow-*`, `--height-*`, `--duration-*`, `--ease-*`, `--animate-*`); 63 of 67 components ported off scoped `<style>` blocks onto utility classes; remaining `:global` rules and `@keyframes` consolidated into one shared `src/renderer-shared/styles/globals.css`.

## Why

The old token names (`--c-*`, `--fs-*`, `--r-*`, …) sat outside Tailwind's `@theme` namespace, so Tailwind utilities couldn't see them and we lived with hand-rolled scoped CSS in every component. Tailwind v4's `@theme` lets us drop most of that CSS in favour of utilities that read straight from the design tokens, which removed ~13k lines of CSS net (−20195 / +7738) and made styling consistent across 100+ files. It also unblocks future work that wants to reuse design tokens via Tailwind classes instead of `var(--…)` everywhere.

Along the way, fixed a few regressions caught during the migration:
- Theme switching in **Preferences → Appearance** stopped repainting app chrome because `appTheme.ts` was still writing under the old `--c-*` prefix; renamed to `--color-*` so the runtime overrides land on the right vars.
- Notch overlay anchor and concave-ear cutouts broke when their `:global(body)` rules moved to the shared file; restored them as a notch-scoped `:global(body)` and added a `globals.css` import to `notch-main.ts`.
- A handful of `class:utility-[arbitrary(value)]` directives broke the Svelte parser (cannot handle parens inside brackets); rewrote them as conditional expressions in the main `class=` attribute.

## How to test

1. `npm run dev` — app must come up cleanly with no compile errors.
2. Spot-check that the chrome looks right on the main window: sidebar, topbar, tabs, status bar, modals (preferences, dialogs), command palette / quick open, onboarding wizard, run-config toolbar, agent inspector, diff/changes panel.
3. **Theme switching**: open Preferences (`⌘,`) → Appearance, click through Default → Dracula → Solarized Light → Nord. Background, accent, hover and focus-ring of the entire app must change with each click; Solarized Light must flip into a true light theme. Check `--color-bg` in devtools Computed for `<html>` to verify.
4. **Notch overlay** (macOS, if `notch.enabled = true`): trigger an active session — the island must grow symmetrically left + right + down (not skewed to the right) and the concave "ears" must cut into the rounded corners.
5. **Remote client**: open Remote Connection from the command palette, scan the QR from a phone or another device on the LAN; verify pairing, terminal mirror, tool picker bottom sheet, soft-keyboard handling.
6. `npm run build` — both `tsc --noEmit` and `svelte-check` must report 0 errors.
7. `npm run lint` — no new warnings.

## Screenshots / recordings

> _Attach before/after of preferences modal, sidebar, status bar, and one or two of the migrated views (changes panel, command palette) to make review faster._

pr.title: refactor(ui): app-wide reskin to unify design language
pr.body:
## What

Reskins almost every surface of the renderer to a single design dialect: `text-text-faint` baseline, `tracking-caps-looser` uppercase section labels, `bg-bg-overlay` popovers, squared `rounded-sm` chips and badges, `size-5` icon buttons, and **fixed-height rows everywhere** to prevent layout shift on hover. Touched surfaces include preferences, sidebar (file tree, git, projects/worktrees), dashboard, status bar, right inspector, diff panel, file editor, and the `Cmd+K` command palette. The branch also closes a long list of accessibility and privacy gaps surfaced by self-review.

## Why

Different surfaces had drifted into different dialects (mixed paddings, mixed badge radii, mixed text-muted vs text-faint baselines), and several high-traffic UIs had cosmetic glitches: layout shifts when hover-revealed actions appeared, summary bars that didn't fill their tracks, alignment mismatches between right-side action columns, and a margin-reset rule in `tokens.css` that silently clobbered every Tailwind margin utility. Bringing the surfaces into one dialect makes the app feel coherent and made it possible to fix the cosmetic issues with shared patterns rather than per-surface bandaids.

The accessibility/privacy track (real `<form>`/`<input>` elements, focus traps, masked secrets, env-shape validation, slugified IDs, focus-visible affordances) was driven by a self-review pass — most of the items there are small targeted fixes rather than redesigns.

## Highlights

- **Visual:** unified section labels, fixed-height rows, squared chips, accent-tint selection (replacing heavy gray flashes), per-category icons in command palette section headers, file-type icons in the sidebar tree, full-bleed active band, hover-revealed inline actions that don't shift the layout.
- **Functional:** new file/folder create from sidebar tree (`fs:createFile` / `fs:mkdir` IPC, walked-up parent validation), git-aware file tree with status letters, welcome dashboard filter + roving keyboard nav, settings export/import surfaced from the prefs sidebar footer.
- **Bugs:** universal margin reset wrapped in `@layer base` so utilities can override it; diff summary bar fills its track; per-row hover doesn't change row height in changes panel and editor toolbar; status-bar buttons don't shift when toggled active.
- **A11y:** real form elements in skill/tool forms, keyboard nav and focus restoration in welcome context menu and `SeparatorPopover`, Tab trapping in Settings dialog with Cmd/Ctrl+K gated to OS, named controls in PrefsRow, focus-revealed profile delete button.
- **Privacy:** SavedPasswords reveal window extended; new env vars masked by default; env JSON shape validated with warnings on secret-named vars; SavedPasswords storage description honest about what's persisted where.
- **Refactor hygiene:** `if/else` chains over discriminated unions replaced with `ts-pattern` (TrackerEditForm); unused styles dropped; large preferences panels split into `_partials/`.

## How to test

1. `npm install && npm run dev`
2. **Unified dialect** — open the app and skim:
   - Sidebar section labels (`PROJECTS`, `WORKTREES`, `GIT`, `FILES`, `TOOLS`) all read at `text-text-faint` with the loose tracking.
   - Right-inspector tabs, dashboard rows, command palette section headers all share the dialect.
3. **Command palette (`Cmd+K`)** — modal radius is `rounded-lg`; magnifier icon in the input; section headers have a leading icon (Wrench / GitCommit / Branch / Panel / Sliders); selected row uses the accent tint, not heavy gray; "Not found in PATH" renders as a squared chip; shortcuts are squared mono chips.
4. **File tree create** — hover a directory → `+` icon appears in the right gutter at a stable column → click → enter `subdir/newfile.ts` → file (and any missing parents) is created. Repeat with the top-level `+` button. Verify "Access denied" never fires for valid in-workspace paths (was broken before this branch).
5. **Layout-shift checks** — hover diff file rows, sidebar rows with action buttons, editor sub-tabs, status bar buttons. Toggle status-bar active states. None should change row height.
6. **Welcome dashboard** — recent-workspace context menu opens with focus on first item; arrow keys cycle; Escape closes and restores focus.
7. **Preferences** — open with `Cmd+,`; Tab cycles only inside the dialog; `Cmd+K` is forwarded to the OS, not captured. Trigger skill install error to verify toast surfaces it.
8. **Privacy** — add a `SECRET=foo` env var → masked by default with a reveal toggle. Paste invalid env JSON → warning surfaces. Open SavedPasswords → reveal countdown is 15s.
9. `npm run typecheck`, `npm run svelte-check`, `npm run lint` — all pass on this branch.

pr.title: fix(terminal): hide cursor during conpty redraws on windows
pr.body:
## What
On Windows, hide the xterm.js cursor during burst writes from ConPTY and re-show it 80ms after output settles, so TUI redraws (claude code, codex, vim) look atomic instead of tracing the cursor across the screen. Also pass `windowsPty: { backend: 'conpty' }` and disable `cursorBlink` on Windows.

## Why
ConPTY scrapes the underlying console buffer and re-emits the screen as a stream of CUP (cursor position) + character runs cell by cell, instead of forwarding the TUI's own escape sequences as Unix PTYs do. xterm renders each CUP synchronously, so users see the caret fly across the screen on every redraw. macOS/Linux are unaffected — the new helper is a passthrough off-Windows.

## How to test
- **macOS/Linux**: `npm run dev`, open a terminal tab, run `vim` / `htop` / `claude`. Behaviour must be identical to today.
- **Windows**: `npm run dev`, run `claude` or `codex`, trigger a full redraw (resize pane, scroll, switch TUI screens). Cursor stays parked during the redraw and reappears once output settles.
- **Windows regression**: type at the PowerShell prompt — cursor still appears normally between keystrokes (80ms debounce releases well within human reaction time).
- **Edge**: Ctrl-C a TUI mid-redraw — cursor reappears within ~80ms even if no further data arrives.

## Checklist

- [x] No changes to non-Windows code paths
- [ ] Manually verified on Windows
- [ ] Manually verified on macOS/Linux

pr.title: fix(remote): enable text selection on mobile terminals
pr.body:
## What
Enable native text selection (long-press → drag → copy) in Canopy Remote terminal views on mobile devices.

## Why
xterm.js selection relies on mouse events which don't fire on touch devices. Users on mobile could only get single-word selection or nothing — no way to select arbitrary text ranges.

## How it works
On touch devices (`@media (pointer: coarse)`), the xterm accessibility tree overlay gets `pointer-events: auto`. This tree is a hidden DOM layer with real terminal text and `user-select: text` — enabling pointer events lets the browser's native long-press selection mechanism work through it. Desktop is unaffected.

pr.title: feat(remote): allow manual selection of LAN network interface
pr.body:
## What

Adds a "Network interface" picker in Settings → Remote Control. When set, the Remote Control signaling server binds only on the chosen interface's IPv4 address (instead of `0.0.0.0`) and the QR pairing URL advertises that same address. "Auto" preserves the previous heuristic (`en0`/`en1` preferred on macOS; first non-virtual adapter elsewhere).

The dropdown groups interfaces as **Auto / Physical / Virtual**. Tunnel/VPN adapters (Tailscale, WireGuard, utun, docker, etc.) — normally filtered out of auto-detect — are listed under "Virtual" so a power user can opt in. A previously-selected interface that has disappeared is shown under "Unavailable" so the user can see what's broken instead of silently snapping back to Auto.

## Why

Auto-detection picks one adapter for the whole machine. On laptops with Wi-Fi + Ethernet, dock-attached NICs, or VPN/tailnet setups, that's often the wrong one — the phone scans the QR, fails to reach the host, and there's no way to override. This makes the binding explicit and works on both Windows and macOS (interface names like `Wi-Fi`/`Ethernet` vs `en0`/`en1` are surfaced verbatim).

When the named interface is no longer present, `start()` returns `NoNetworkInterface` (existing user-facing error); listen mode silently no-ops, matching the existing pattern. Changing the preference while a session is running stops it so the next pairing or trusted reconnect picks up the new bind — mirrors the existing `remote.enabled=false` teardown.

## How to test

1. Open Settings → Remote Control. Pick `Wi-Fi` (Windows) / `en0` (macOS) from the new "Network interface" dropdown.
2. Open the command palette → "Remote Connection". Confirm the QR URL contains the IP of the chosen adapter.
3. On Windows: `netstat -an | findstr <port>` shows LISTENING only on the picked IP, not `0.0.0.0`. On macOS: `lsof -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN -P` confirms the same.
4. Switch the dropdown to a different physical adapter while the modal is open — session stops, reopen modal and verify new IP in the QR.
5. Select a virtual interface (e.g. Tailscale) — bind happens on its IP; peer from the same tailnet can pair.
6. Set the preference to a name that doesn't exist (via DevTools / preferences edit) — `start()` returns `NoNetworkInterface` with "No usable network interface found on the LAN".
7. Regression: leave the dropdown on "Auto (detect at start)" — pairing works exactly as before.

## Screenshots / recordings

_To be added during review (Windows + macOS Settings screenshots)._

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [x] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default) — the existing `remote.enabled` gate still applies; this is a sub-setting of an already opt-in feature

- [x] Keyboard accessible (all interactive elements reachable via keyboard) — reuses existing `CustomSelect` which supports full keyboard nav

pr.title: fix(worktree): allow creation paths under home dir on Windows
pr.body:
## Summary

- Worktree creation on Windows fails with `Access denied: path outside workspace`. The 2026-05-22 audit wired `validateCreationPath` into `git:worktreeAdd` / `git:worktreeCheckout`, but worktrees are intentionally created OUTSIDE the workspace (default `worktrees.baseDir` is `~/canopy/worktrees`). On Windows the home dir is never a workspace ancestor, so every creation gets rejected.
- New `validateWorktreeCreationPath` keeps the TOCTOU-safe ancestor walk and escape-via-`..` rejection from `validateCreationPath`, but relaxes containment to **home OR workspace**. System locations like `/etc` or `C:\Program Files` remain blocked.
- `git:worktreeRemove` switches to the matching `validateWorktreeExistingPath` — `WindowManager` only exposes the *active* worktree, so removing inactive ones hit the same wall.

## Test plan

pr.title: refactor(terminal): replace local websocket bridge with ipc
pr.body:
## What

Replaces the local terminal WebSocket bridge with an Electron IPC-based PTY stream service. Local xterm rendering now subscribes to PTY data through preload IPC, while remote terminal forwarding uses the same IPC stream and sends data onward over the existing remote channel.

Also hardens remote terminal replay by checking stale PTY stream availability and adding xterm write backpressure so large replay bursts do not flood xterm's internal write buffer.

## Why

Local desktop terminal traffic does not need a WebSocket server and should use Electron's native process boundary instead. This removes local port/server overhead, keeps renderer Node access behind preload, and avoids performance issues during terminal replay or remote reconnect races.

1. Run `npm run typecheck:node`.

5. Start the app and open a local terminal; verify input/output, resize, tab switching, and terminal history replay still work.
6. Pair a remote client and open a terminal; verify output streams, reconnecting does not produce `PTY stream does not exist`, and large replay/output bursts remain responsive.

pr.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #263, completing the dependency-security pass.

### `build(deps)`: bump @babel/core to 7.29.7 (root)
Resolves the low-severity arbitrary-file-read advisory (`<= 7.29.0`) in `@babel/core` (transitive via electron-vite). Lockfile-only, within the existing `^7` range. **Root `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities.** Build verified (`npm run build`, exit 0).

### `ci`: grouped dependabot configuration
Weekly **grouped** (minor+patch) npm updates for `/`, `/mobile`, and github-actions, so the backlog stops recurring as a pile of single alerts.

- **Mobile ignores `expo` / `expo-*` / `react` / `react-dom` / `react-native` / `react-native-*`** — these are Expo SDK-pinned and must move together via an SDK bump. A stray `react-native` 0.83→0.86 minor is exactly what contaminated grouped PR #263.
- **Review gate kept** (chosen deliberately): a maintainer still applies `claude:review:approved` before auto-merge.

### Deferred / residual (mobile, build-time, low risk)
- Mobile `@babel/core` (low) and `@expo/xcpretty → js-yaml` (moderate) are **left to Dependabot's next run** — hand-fixing dragged ~500 lines of pre-existing metro/hermes lockfile drift into the diff, obscuring the security change. With RN/Expo now ignored, Dependabot will produce a clean, CI-validated mobile PR.
- `@istanbuljs/load-nyc-config → js-yaml@3.x` (moderate, jest coverage, **not runtime-reachable**): no upstream 3.x patch exists and `load-nyc-config` requires the js-yaml 3 API, so forcing 4.x would break it. **Recommend dismissing this Dependabot alert** (tolerable risk / no fix available).

## What

Rebuilds the task-tracker experience end to end:

- **Configuration split into two clear surfaces** — Settings hosts only *Your connections* (personal, full CRUD, authoritative token management); a dedicated **Project tracker modal** (per active worktree) connects repo-configured trackers and edits branch/PR naming **per board** (read-only rows with rendered examples, in-place editing with Cancel/Done, board overrides, reset to built-in defaults). - **Credential verification** — stored tokens are checked against the tracker API on config load; expired/revoked tokens surface a *Credentials expired* badge with a Reconnect action (modal, Settings, sidebar) instead of showing as connected forever. OS-aware storage note (DPAPI/Keychain/keyring).
- **Hybrid template editor** — `{field}` placeholders are draggable chips, everything between them is plain text edited in place (any separator works). Dropped the `{?var}…{/var}` conditional; empty fields now render to nothing and remove their preceding separator.
- **Branch creation** — the proposed branch name is editable before creation (sanitized like rendered templates), with regenerate-from-template.
- **Task panel (right Inspector, new "Task" tab)** — header (key link, status, assignee, description), **workflow-aware status change** (Jira introspects required fields/resolutions via `transitions?expand=transitions.fields`; YouTrack applies via Commands API with server errors surfaced; GitHub close/reopen + state reason), and the **comment history** with add-comment. - **Picker** — assignee chip per row (highlighted when it's you).
- Fixes: activeTask pref key separator mismatch (never reloaded on Windows), worktree config load during startup restore, confirmations rendering above open modals, dev-only vite 7 IPv6 bind regression.

Config scope (per-repo vs personal) and precedence were opaque; credentials looked connected after expiring; there was no way to manage a task (status/comment) from the worktree bound to it.

- **Task panel (right Inspector "Task" tab)** — header (key link, type icon, status, assignee avatar, description, image attachments with thumbnails), workflow-aware status change, comment history with add-comment, agent hand-off; deleted tasks get a dedicated "not found" state with honest unlink rules.
- **In-tracker task creation** (`NewTaskForm`, shared) — Create Worktree gains a **New task** mode (one click creates the task AND the worktree; pre-create branch-name draft with a highlighted `{taskKey}` placeholder) and the link dialog gains **Existing tasks / New task** tabs (single-select + confirm; created tasks auto-link). ## Why

Config scope (per-repo vs personal) and precedence were opaque; credentials looked connected after expiring; tasks could only be picked, not created; and there was no way to manage a task (status/comment) from the worktree bound to it.

pr.title: fix(workspace): normalize path separators to stop ghost session windows
pr.body:
## What

Fixes the "Canopy always opens in two windows" bug: an extra ghost window re-appeared on every launch and closing it never helped.

- **Root cause:** workspace paths were persisted in whatever separator style they arrived in — native dialogs produce `C:\source\repo`, git and the renderer produce `C:/source/repo` — so the same directory could get **two rows in `workspaces`**. Layouts stranded under the stale duplicate were invisible to the close-time cleanup (`getByPath` compares exact strings, always hitting the other row), and session restore treats "workspace has layouts but is in no window config" as a window to re-spawn. Result: an un-killable ghost window.
- **Fix:** new `normalizeWorkspacePath()` (forward slashes) applied at the storage boundary — `WorkspaceStore.getByPath`/`upsert`, `LayoutStore.save`/`get`/`delete`, `WindowManager` path tracking, and the restore-time config-vs-layouts comparison.
- **Migration 11** heals existing databases: normalizes `workspace_layouts.worktree_path` (deduping to the newest row), merges duplicate workspace rows — keeping the most recently opened one, repointing `workspace_layouts` and `skill_definitions` (both FK CASCADE) — then rewrites `workspaces.path` canonically.
- `vitest.config.ts` now also includes `src/main/**/*.test.ts` (pure helpers only), a first step toward the main-process regression coverage requested in #324's review.

## Why

Reported from live usage: two independent windows on every start, with the ghost window impossible to get rid of (its layouts could never be deleted). Confirmed in a real profile: `workspaces` held both `C:\source\...\ThesisSupervising` and `C:/source/.../ThesisSupervising`, with layouts under the stale backslash row.

## How to test

1. Seed the disease into a dev profile (`%APPDATA%/canopy-dev/canopy.db`): two workspace rows for one directory differing only in separator style, a `workspace_layouts` row under the older one, `openWindowConfigs` mentioning only another project.
2. `npm run dev` — migration 11 merges the rows and repoints the layouts (verify in the DB); the restored window for the orphaned layouts opens one last, legitimate time.
3. Close that window → its layouts row is now actually deleted (this was the broken part).
4. Relaunch → single window; the ghost is gone.
5. `npm test` (72 tests), `npm run build`, `npm run lint`.

Verified e2e exactly this way on a seeded dev profile (steps 1–5), plus the pre-fix code was confirmed to reproduce the ghost with the same seed.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, or credentials logged or stored in plaintext
- [ ] Non-core feature is behind a feature flag (off by default) — n/a, bugfix
- [x] Cross-platform: no hardcoded OS-specific labels, paths, or shell commands
